question: India is set to invest over US$360 billion in renewable energy and infrastructure by .
solution:
The correct answer is __**2030**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's renewable energy investment:** India has committed to investing over **US$360 billion** in renewable energy and infrastructure by the year **2030** to achieve its climate goals and energy transition targets.
 
• The government aims to achieve **500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity** by 2030, as announced during the **2021 United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP26)**.
 
• This investment aligns with India’s **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** under the Paris Agreement to reduce the carbon intensity of its GDP by **33-35% by 2030** compared to 2005 levels.
 
• India is focusing on developing **solar energy, wind energy, green hydrogen, and energy storage systems** as part of its renewable energy strategy.
 
• The government has also introduced policies like the **Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme** for solar manufacturing to support the renewable energy sector and meet the 2030 targets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Paris Agreement and Nationally Determined Contributions:**

 
 
• India is a signatory to the **Paris Agreement**, which aims to limit global temperature rise to below 2°C above pre-industrial levels.
 
• Under the agreement, India has pledged to achieve **40% of its installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel sources by 2030**.
 
• The government has also committed to creating an additional carbon sink of **2.5–3 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent through forest and tree cover** by 2030.
 
 
 
• **India's Renewable Energy Initiatives:**
 
 
• India is the third-largest producer of renewable energy globally and has set ambitious targets to **reduce dependence on fossil fuels**.
 
• Key initiatives include the **National Solar Mission**, **Wind Energy Programme**, and **National Green Hydrogen Mission**.
 
• India's current renewable energy capacity is around **175 GW**, and it is expected to reach **500 GW by 2030**.
 
 
 
• **Green Hydrogen Mission:**
 
 
• Launched in **2022**, the Green Hydrogen Mission aims to make India a global hub for green hydrogen production.
 
• It supports the production of **hydrogen through renewable energy sources**, reducing carbon emissions in industries like steel and cement.
 
• The mission involves creating **export opportunities for green hydrogen** and aims to achieve **5 million tonnes annual production** by 2030.
 
 
 
• **International Collaboration:**
 
 
• India collaborates with countries like the **United States**, **Germany**, and **Australia** for renewable energy projects.
 
• Global initiatives like the **International Solar Alliance (ISA)**, founded by India and France, promote solar energy deployment worldwide.
 
• India has secured funding from international organizations like the **World Bank** and **Asian Development Bank** for renewable energy infrastructure.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Challenges in Renewable Energy Development:**

 
 
• India faces challenges in renewable energy development, including **land acquisition issues**, **grid connectivity**, and **high costs of advanced technology**.
 
• The transition to renewable energy also requires skilled manpower and better **policy frameworks**.
 
• Despite these challenges, the government is working on regulatory reforms and financial incentives to boost investment.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Environmental Benefits:**
 
 
• Investing in renewable energy will help reduce India's dependence on **imported fossil fuels**, improving **energy security**.
 
• It will also create **employment opportunities** in sectors like solar manufacturing, installation, and maintenance.
 
• Renewable energy plays a crucial role in achieving **sustainable development** by reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
